questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The courses in the marine environment.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It went over all my expectations. Everyone was speaking English and I met a lot of exchange/Dutch students. The culture and atmosphere in Wageningen is unique and I would not have chosen differently.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. Everything was online and the student advisor was very good at responding to any questions. She was really good at advising which courses to take.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I signed up for AID (introduction) in July where they advised me and helped me settle in. I also got a couple of emails where I received some instructions about my arrival etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Use
room.nl
but be patient. I received a room in mid-July and had to arrive in Wageningen at the beginning of August.
I lived in Bornsesteegl but I cannot recommend it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Wageningen is very small so off-campus (Bornsesteeg) is only 5 minutes away.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was all online which was really good and the exchange coordinator was really helpful.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Course coordinator, websites, and excel sheets.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I did not have any diffuculties.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look into the minors, then you don't need to look into assumed knowledge for all your courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took a minor which is a set of courses with a specific topic. You can take them on your master's and bachelor's because they are part of your electives.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There was less homework but the days were longer. The lunch breaks were 2 hours long where you could meet up with friends or go do sports. The professors were very welcoming and the teaching methods were in general good. Maybe a bit too much group work with different people.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Introduction to bioinformatics, marine systems, sustainable seaweed chains, seaweed biology cultivation and biology, and circularity in aquatic food systems

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Marine systems were really interesting if you like biology, social science, and the marine environment. There was a good excursion to other parts of the Netherlands.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You have to pay for your own router. You need a bike and if you live at Bornsesteeg then you need to pay for your own stove and kitchen equipment.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: phone and public transportation.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I went to rugby which was really fun (Wageningen Rugby Club). I also had a subscription for the sports center de Bongerd, AID, Erasmus social network (ESN), and ISOW. There are plenty of clubs and cultural events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The rugby club was really fun and the introduction (AID).

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I personally really liked Den Hague but also travel to other neighboring countries.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was really easy. Danish and Dutch cultures are very similar.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Start to rugby.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The people are very direct and training starts very late.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Everything was so close and people are very direct.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Join AID, don't live at Bornsesteeg, and go to the market in the city center.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The Rhein (the river) is very nice in the summer.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: When I learned to drive my bike without my hands.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting a Dutch bank account

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
